newsitem.title: USA: BPA says will buy spot power to cover Friday needs.
newsitem.headline: BPA says will buy spot power to cover Friday needs.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) will be in the spot market to cover short positions for Friday during peak demand hours, trade sources at the federal power marketing agency said Thursday.
"We are still facing flood control restrictions. We are definitely short," said a trader at BPA.
He noted newly-imposed discharge restrictions at some headwater hydropower projects such as the Libby, Hungry Horse and Dworshak dams were limiting power supplies.
The BPA trader said estimates that the agency purchased about 1,000 megawatts (MW) for Thursday pre-schedulings were "not far from the truth."

The trader said BPA continued to offer non-firm power for hours ending at 0600 and 2300 PDT on Friday at $9.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) for both Northwest and COB deliveries, while delivered prices for hours ending 0100-0500 and 2400 were flat at $9.00.
Firm power during off-peak hours on Friday was also unchanged at $9.00 per MWh for all deliveries.
